text:
Claire Li: PartnerCloud engineering asked for a tiny, production‑like example they can import into their marketplace CI. Requirements: single Terraform module (marketplace_shim), tiny example app (FastAPI), multi‑arch notes (arm64 + x86), optional KMS, CI that runs a smoke deploy + curl, and an Apache-2.0 LICENSE. Keep it <200 LOC for examples.
Ravi Patel: OK. Proposal: create a new repo `marketplace-lite-refkit` that reuses our internal refkit modules via git submodule (or registry) so we don't copy heavy code. One module = simplest surface area for partners.
Diego Morales: I'll sketch the module API. Minimal vars: name, image, region, arch (arm|x86), enable_kms (bool). We'll provide a var map for instance_type_by_arch and a simple lookup. No provider trickery.
Maya Chen: Also include an example KMS block and an audit sink placeholder. Make the KMS optional (off by default) and document compliance notes for the partner security reviewers.
Jordan Lee: For the FastAPI example, keep it to a single endpoint /health and /invoke that POSTs a little JSON to a stubbed model endpoint. Dockerfile should be tiny and use python:3.11-slim. Add requirements.txt with fastapi and uvicorn.
Claire Li: Good. Can we also include a signed module registry publish note and semver guidance? Partner wants to know how to pin provider versions and how to roll minor updates.
Ravi Patel: Yes. Add a short section in docs/README.md describing: 1) version pinning example in required_providers and module source syntax, 2) how to create a release tag and publish to terraform registry (or vendor).
Diego Morales: Draft main.tf snippet for module: 
```
# modules/marketplace_shim/main.tf
terraform {
  required_providers {
    partner = { source = "partnercloud/partner" version = ">= 1.0, < 2.0" }
  }
}
variable "arch" { type = string default = "x86" }
variable "enable_kms" { type = bool default = false }
locals { instance_map = { arm = "c7g.large" x86 = "c6i.large" } }
resource "partner_market_listing" "listing" {
  name = var.name
  image = var.image
  instance_type = local.instance_map[var.arch]
  region = var.region
}
resource "partner_kms_key" "optional" {
  count = var.enable_kms ? 1 : 0
  purpose = "ENCRYPTION"
}
output "listing_id" { value = partner_market_listing.listing.id }
```
Jordan Lee: Example Dockerfile snippet for examples/fastapi/Dockerfile:
```
FROM python:3.11-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt ./
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
COPY app.py ./
CMD ["uvicorn", "app:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8080"]
```
Maya Chen: CI: simple GitHub Actions smoke.yml that: checks out, sets up terraform, runs fmt + tflint, terraform init/plan (apply with auto-approve for a tiny test workspace), then runs curl http://example-app:8080/health (we can use docker-compose in CI or spin the container). Fail fast on diffs.
Ravi Patel: Add .tflint.hcl, terraform.lock.hcl committed, and a small unit-test script that uses `terratest` style shell checks (but avoid heavy deps). Keep the smoke test as bash `terraform apply` -> curl -> terraform destroy.
Claire Li: Partner asked for a one‑page onboarding: fork -> update provider pins -> run smoke CI -> submit PR -> notify Redwood for verification. Add that as docs/ONBOARDING.md. Also include a short limitations matrix (regions, CPU/GPU SKUs, no special driver GPUs).
Diego Morales: I'll prepare the PR tomorrow. I'll aim for: modules/marketplace_shim/{main.tf,variables.tf,outputs.tf}, examples/fastapi/{app.py,requirements.txt,Dockerfile}, ci/smoke.yml, docs/{README.md,ONBOARDING.md,COMPLIANCE.md}, LICENSE, .tflint.hcl, terraform.lock.hcl.
Jordan Lee: I'll write the tiny app.py now and keep it ~40 LOC. app.invoke will echo back the payload with a fake "model_output". We'll explicitly document that secrets should come from provider/KMS and never be hardcoded.
partner-bot: Helpful checklist: https://redwood-internal/partner-checklists/marketplace-lite (auto-post)
Maya Chen: Let's also include a short matrix example in README for instance_type_by_arch and a sample vars.tfvars for CI. That speeds partner onboarding.
Claire Li: Great. Who owns the final review? Ravi + Maya?
Ravi Patel: I'll do the module review, Maya does security/KMS docs. Diego will own the initial PR and tag us.
Diego Morales: Roger. PR link will be posted here once created. If partner wants a live walkthrough, propose 30m pairing after PR review. :calendar: 
Claire Li: Thanks team. Keep examples tiny and dependency-free. We'll attach the onboarding doc to the partner ticket once PR is merged.
